GeoData Specimen maps to the iSamples top-level sample class
Both are primary identifiers; gd:specimen_id allows local strings while iSamples uses URIs
Both slots hold a persistent registered identifier (IGSN URI)
Both describe where the specimen was collected
Date/time of collection
Person or org responsible for collection
Both use iSamples Material vocabulary terms as values
Hierarchical sample relationship (subsample, aliquot)
Holding institution
Physical storage location within repository
ENVO water is broader; mat:liquidwater is specific to liquid phase
Freshwater is a subtype of liquid water
Seawater is a subtype of liquid water
Groundwater is a subtype of liquid water
Pore water is a subtype of liquid water
Air is the primary instance of gaseous material in earth science
Atmosphere broadly corresponds to gaseous material
Glacial/sea ice maps to iSamples anyice
Snow is a form of frozen water
Permafrost is frozen soil/sediment; no exact iSamples equivalent
Biota broadly corresponds to organic material
rock, sediment, sediment_core, ice_core, soil, mineral, speleothem all map here
